clue.text: Bar for some ladies to patronise

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A pub bar aimed at attracting female customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points into 'ladiES TO Patronise'; 'Bar' looks like a pub but is the legal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to estop is to preclude or prevent someone from asserting something, i.e. to bar them.

clue.text: Bears arms possibly to cause confusion

indicators.note: possibly says these letters might form another word when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone carrying weapons might well alarm people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges BEARS ARMS.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass someone is to make them awkward and flustered.

clue.text: Artist absorbed by bird's distinguishing feature

indicators.note: absorbed by says the artist goes inside the bird

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter fascinated by a bird's characteristic markings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbed by' is the container signal; RA, a Royal Academician, is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A trait is a characteristic quality that marks someone out.

clue.text: Fussiness of a journalist in a food store

indicators.note: in says the journalist goes inside the food store

parts.note: a pantry is a cupboard or room for food
ED, editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter being finicky in a larder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; ED, an editor, is the usual crossword journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedantry is excessive concern with minor details and rules.

clue.text: Buys tea in bags

indicators.note: in says the word for tea sits inside the word for bags

parts.note: purses are small bags
cha (or char) is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up tea sold in bags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the surface suggests teabags, but bags are purses and cha is slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: To buy something is to acquire it by payment, the verb sense of making a purchase.

clue.text: Noble and quiet always

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: An aristocrat who is forever silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility such as a duke or earl.

clue.text: Came down after a nap subdued

indicators.note: after says the word for came down follows the word for a nap

parts.note: a rest is a short nap
it rained, came down from the sky

explanation.surface: After a snooze, someone came downstairs in a quiet mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Came down is rain falling, not descending stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Restrained behaviour is held back and muted.

clue.text: Rough though sound beast

indicators.note: sound says the word for beast is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a horse is a beast

explanation.surface: An animal that is tough yet healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like healthy, as in sound in wind and limb, but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoarse voice is harsh and grating, rough in tone.

clue.text: A sheepish creature, shy when receiving judge

indicators.note: receiving says the word for shy takes the word for judge inside it

parts.note: to shy is to throw, as is to sling
a judge hears a case

explanation.surface: A timid animal, nervous when meeting a magistrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shy' looks like timid but means throw; 'receiving' puts the judge's verb inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearling is a young sheep that has been shorn once.

clue.text: Two ways to break in

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
AVE is short for avenue, another way

explanation.surface: There are a couple of methods of breaking into somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: ways are roads: ST and AVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To stave in a cask or boat is to smash a hole in it.

clue.text: Lack of taste and point in worship

indicators.note: in says the words for and and point go inside the word for worship

parts.note: to bless is to praise or worship
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A complaint that a church service has no flavour or purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; point is a compass point, north.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insipid with no flavour or character is described as bland.

clue.text: Building near a field

indicators.note: building means putting the letters of the following words together into something new

explanation.surface: A building located close to a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building' looks like a noun but signals that NEAR A is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A field of activity or contest is an arena, as in the political arena.

clue.text: Valuing the metal in scrap

indicators.note: in says the word for the metal goes inside the word for scrap

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
tin is a metal

explanation.surface: Assessing how much metal there is in some scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the metal is the scrap-yard sort, but scrap here is a piece of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rating something is assessing or appraising its worth.

clue.text: Keep a little cash to make a booking

parts.note: P, a penny, is a small amount of money
a reserve is an act of reserving, a booking

explanation.surface: Holding back some money to pay for a reservation.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for penny; 'to make' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to maintain or retain it, so keep is a synonym.

clue.text: There's no strong drink — it's discouraged

parts.note: spirit is strong alcoholic drink
the suffix less means without, so no

explanation.surface: Someone is downhearted because the bar has run out of liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Strong drink with no added: SPIRIT followed by LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiritless means lacking courage or energy, downcast.

clue.text: A worker hid poor output — so like the man!

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker in crosswords

indicators.note: output means the letters of hid poor are put out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An employee concealed shoddy work, which is just what a man would do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'output' rearranges HID POOR; the exclamation 'so like the man' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthropoid means resembling a human being in form, especially of apes.

clue.text: Youngsters agree nets can be used

indicators.note: can be used says these letters are to be reshaped into another word

explanation.surface: Young people consent that the nets may be put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be used' rearranges AGREE NETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are young people aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: One has infiltrated through a mole

indicators.note: has infiltrated says the letter for one gets inside the word for through

parts.note: per means through or by means of
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spy has got in by means of an undercover agent.
explanation.walkthrough: A mole here is a breakwater, not a spy or animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A mole is a stone jetty or breakwater, a structure projecting into the sea.

clue.text: Telling 2 dn? Certainly not!

parts.note: asks whether a characteristic is that of speaking out; the opposite, a disposition to keep quiet, is meant

explanation.definitionFit: Reticence is a reluctance to reveal thoughts or feelings, a habit of keeping silent.

clue.text: A sporting event that is boring people

parts.note: flat means dull or boring
a race is a people or nation

explanation.surface: A dull sports occasion with tedious spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat race is a horse race with no jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse racing over level ground without hurdles is a sport event.

clue.text: Notice a large number appear.

parts.note: to notice is to see
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Spotting a big crowd turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: To seem is to give the impression or look a certain way, as appear does.

clue.text: Fresh and amusing, which is what one has to go on

definitions.text: what one has to go on

parts.note: green means fresh or new
light entertainment is amusing rather than serious

explanation.surface: Something new and entertaining is the signal to proceed.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on traffic signals: you need it to go.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic signals show the go colour as permission to proceed, so it is what one needs before moving.

clue.text: Card game — could be pontoon

definitions.meaning: a trick-taking game for four players with partners
a pontoon is a floating structure carrying a road across water

explanation.definitionFit: Contract and auction are forms of the card game, and a pontoon is a floating crossing over a river.

clue.text: Expedition to the French metropolis — both sides of the river

parts.note: a la is French for to the

indicators.note: both sides of says the city lies on each side of the river letter

parts.note: a metropolis is a city
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A trip to a French city that straddles a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Expedition here means promptness, not a journey; R goes inside CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition in its older sense is speed or promptness, and alacrity is eager readiness.

clue.text: Prize-fighting in the present era

indicators.note: in says the fighting is placed inside the present era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, is the present era
war is fighting

explanation.surface: Boxing for money in modern times.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash breaks 'Prize-fighting': Prize is the definition, fighting is WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is a prize given for merit.

clue.text: Stable or attics for conversion

indicators.note: converting the word attics means remaking its letters into a new word

explanation.surface: Weighing a stable against attics as candidates for a property conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' looks like a horse's building but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something static stays fixed and unchanging, so it is steady.

clue.text: Magistrate making rebel leader get into line

indicators.note: get into says the letter goes inside the word for line

parts.note: a tier is a row or line

indicators.note: leader of rebel means its first letter

explanation.surface: A judge makes the head of the rebellion fall into line.
explanation.walkthrough: R (first of rebel) goes inside TIER; a trier is one who tries cases.
explanation.definitionFit: A trier is one who tries a case, as a judge or magistrate does.

clue.text: Express satisfaction in a catty sort of way

definitions.text: Express satisfaction in a catty sort of way

parts.words: Express satisfaction in a catty sort of way
parts.note: catty suggests spiteful remarks, but it means literally as a cat does when content

explanation.definitionFit: Cats make a low vibrating sound when pleased.

clue.text: A capital forward!

parts.note: the capital of a column is its head or top

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic cry praising an excellent forward player.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital as an exclamation of approval misleads; it is the top of a column.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front or further on is to be forward.

clue.text: Competing with a Greek character in high spirits

indicators.note: in says the Greek letter sits inside the word for high spirits

parts.note: elation is a state of high spirits
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Taking part in a contest against a cheerful Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' means a letter, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulation is the effort to equal or surpass others, a form of rivalry.

clue.text: A person qualified to work on prescribed lines

definitions.text: A person qualified to work on prescribed lines

parts.words: A person qualified to work on prescribed lines
parts.note: seems to describe a rule-follower, but prescribed refers to a doctor's prescriptions made up by a chemist

explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist who makes up medicines from prescriptions is a qualified dispensing chemist.

clue.text: About a quarter turned back, and that's really odd

parts.note: E, east, is a quarter of the compass

indicators.note: turned back says the word for about is read in reverse

parts.note: re means about or concerning
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Something turned back about a quarter of the way is weird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned back' reverses RE to ER; that's is i.e.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie means strange and unsettling, uncannily weird.
